extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners preparing or prosecuting reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and preparation of reissue (including divisional/continuation/continuation-in-part) applications, focusing on oaths/declarations, assignee consents, error statements, amendments, claim/drawing procedures, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP acceptance of copy of reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a divisional or continuation reissue application is filed with a copy of the oath/declaration from the parent reissue application, OPAP should accept the copy as an oath/declaration and accord a filing date so long as all other filing requirements are met, even though it may be improper under 35 U.S.C. 251 or 37 CFR 1.175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although OPAP accepts the copy for filing purposes, the examiner must still review compliance with statutory/regulatory requirements. If the copy does not comply with applicable 37 CFR provisions (see other criteria), the examiner should reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require a new oath/declaration (and possibly a new assignee consent). See MPEP § 1410.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.175(f)(1) — when a copy of inventor’s oath/declaration satisfies requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuing reissue application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) may satisfy the inventor’s oath/declaration requirement by a copy of the inventor’s oath/declaration from the earlier-filed reissue application provided that: (i) the inventor (or each joint inventor) executed an inventor’s oath/declaration for the earlier-filed reissue application (except as provided in § 1.64); (ii) the continuing reissue application does not seek to enlarge the scope of the claims of the original patent; or (iii) the application for the original patent was filed under § 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should verify each subcondition. If any condition is not met, the copy does not satisfy the requirement and a new oath/declaration is required. See also the interplay with 37 CFR 1.175(f)(2) regarding identification of errors relied upon for reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.175(f)(2) — identification of reissuable error when prior errors no longer relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If all errors identified in the inventor’s oath/declaration from the earlier-filed reissue application are no longer being relied upon as the basis for reissue, the applicant must identify an error being relied upon as the basis for reissue (i.e., the copy alone is insufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the error in remarks is insufficient unless a proper reissuable error was previously entered in the initial oath/declaration. Thus, where prior-identified errors are not being relied on, a new or supplemental oath/declaration identifying an error is required; the examiner should reject if this is not done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner rejection when copy of oath/declaration does not comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If the copy of the oath or declaration from the parent reissue application does not comply with 37 CFR 1.175(f)(1) (or pre-AIA 1.175(e) where applicable), the examiner should reject the claims of the continuing reissue application under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being based on a defective oath/declaration and require a new oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should also check whether the error statement in the copy covers an error being corrected in the continuing reissue application; if not, require new oath/declaration and a new assignee consent as appropriate. See MPEP § 1414 and § 1410.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175(e) — continuing reissue applications before Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175(e), the requirement for the inventor’s oath/declaration for a continuing reissue application may be satisfied by a copy of the earlier-filed reissue oath/declaration only when the continuing reissue application replaces its parent reissue application; otherwise the continuing application must include its own oath/declaration identifying at least one error in the original patent not corrected by the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a continuing reissue application filed before Sept 16, 2012 corrects the same error in a different way than its parent, different oaths/declarations must be presented in the two reissue applications. Also, if a preliminary amendment corrects an error not covered by the parent's oath, a supplemental oath/declaration pursuant to pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) will be required. See MPEP §§ 1414 and 1414.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error statement must identify an error being corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should check the copy of the oath/declaration to ensure that it identifies an error being corrected by the continuing (i.e., divisional or continuation) reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For divisional reissue applications, the copy may or may not cover the error because a divisional is directed to a new invention. If the copy does not cover an error being corrected, reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require a new oath/declaration and a new assignee consent if needed. For apps filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, identification in remarks is insufficient unless there was a proper reissuable error previously entered in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent copy acceptability in continuation reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation reissue application filed with a copy of the assignee consent from the parent reissue application and a newly executed reissue oath/declaration generally: the copy of the assignee consent from the parent is not acceptable unless the continuation corrects an error for which consent was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a new oath/declaration is indicative of correction of a different error. Under such circumstances, OPAP will accord a filing date, and the examiner should reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require a new consent. See MPEP § 1410.02. Examiners should compare the consent and the error statements to determine coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance by OPAP of copies for filing date vs substantive compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a continuation reissue application is filed with a copy of the assignee consent and a copy of the oath/declaration from the parent reissue application, OPAP should accept the copies and accord a filing date so long as all other filing requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance for filing does not mean the documents substantively satisfy regulatory requirements — substantive review by the examiner is required and may result in rejection or requests for new documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of all patent claims in parent and continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the claims of the patent to be reissued must be presented in both the parent reissue application and the continuation reissue application in some form (amended, unamended, or canceled). The same claim of the patent cannot be presented for examination in both the parent and continuation reissue as a pending claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any added claims must be numbered beginning with the next highest number following the original patent claims. If the same claim appears pending in both, see the treatment discussed for divisional reissues and consider corrective amendments or rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting considerations for parent/continuation reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the parent reissue application issues before examination of the continuation, or where parent and continuation are examined together, the continuation’s claims should be reviewed for double patenting over the parent; a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection should be made as to any overlapping claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider terminal disclaimer to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection; a terminal disclaimer ensures common ownership under 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3) or common enforcement under 37 CFR 1.321(d)(3) for the remainder of the unexpired term. See MPEP § 804 - § 804.05 and In re Berg/In re Graff guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE availability for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 is available for a reissue application for reissue of a utility or plant patent filed on or after June 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE continues prosecution of the existing reissue application and is not a filing of a new reissue application; an RCE filing will not be announced in the Official Gazette. If merged with a reexamination proceeding, filing an RCE will not automatically dissolve the merger; examine merger decision for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reissue applications must comply with 37 CFR 1.173 and 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the description and claims in reissue applications must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.173; amendments may be made by incorporation into the specification upon filing (with markings per paragraph (d)) or by a separate amendment paper complying with the specified format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If made by amendment paper, the paper must direct specified changes and include full texts where required. The exception for examiner’s amendments under 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply in reissue applications. Use form paragraph 14.20.01 to advise applicants of proper manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for changes (brackets and underlining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reissued that are made to the specification, including the claims but excluding certain large tables/listings, must include: (1) matter to be omitted enclosed in brackets; and (2) matter to be added underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent (or the patent as changed by prior proceedings as required by 37 CFR 1.173(g)). For patents that already have markings from earlier reissues or reexaminations, double brackets/double underlining conventions apply to distinguish changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments — full paragraph submission and location identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification (other than the claims, certain tables/listings, or drawings) must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph, including markings, and the precise point in the specification where the added/rewritten paragraph is located must be identified. An entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presenting the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All newly added paragraphs must be submitted completely underlined each time they are re-submitted; bracketing/underlining is always relative to the original patent text, not relative to prior amendment versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment presentation and support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each claim being changed and each claim being added; for each claim changed, a parenthetical such as 'amended' should follow the claim number. A claim canceled may be canceled by a statement. Each amendment must be accompanied by the status (pending or canceled) of all patent claims and all added claims as of the date of the amendment, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure for the claim changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supply claim status or an explanation of support will generally result in a notification that the amendment before final rejection is not completely responsive (see 37 CFR 1.135(c)); an amendment after final rejection will not be entered. New claims added must be presented completely underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of patent claims preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. A patent claim retains its original number even if canceled in the reissue proceeding; numbering of any added claims must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure added claim numbers begin after the last original patent claim number; do not reuse numbers of canceled original claims for new claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment may not enlarge scope or introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.173(a), no amendment in a reissue application may enlarge the scope of the claims unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent. Further, the amendment may not introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should verify time limits for enlarging claim scope (see MPEP § 1412.03) and check for new matter in the amendment; improper enlargements or new matter require appropriate rejection or requirement for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to patent drawings must be submitted as replacement sheets of drawings (37 CFR 1.173(b)(3)). Any replacement sheet must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and include all figures appearing on the original sheet, even if only one figure is amended. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures enclosed in brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' All changes must be explained in detail on a separate sheet accompanying the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up annotated copy of amended drawing figures may be included and must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Marked-up Drawings.' If required by the examiner, a marked-up copy must be provided. See MPEP § 1413 for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: All changes must be made vis-à-vis the patent to be reissued
rubrics_metrics.description: All underlining and bracketing in the reissue application must be made relative to the text of the patent in effect as of the date of filing of the reissue application (which includes earlier changes made by reexamination certificates, prior reissue, certificates of correction, PTAB certificates, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first amendment must be made relative to the patent as changed by prior proceedings if any; subsequent amendments must continue to be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of filing date, not relative to prior amendments in the reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for formulas/equations already containing markings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original or previously changed patent includes a formula or equation already having underlining or bracketing as part of the formula, any amendment should bracket the entire formula and rewrite and totally underline the amended formula in the re-presented paragraph; segments of a formula should not be amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original patent includes prior bracketing/underlining from earlier reissue, use double brackets and double underlining to distinguish the present changes. When the reissue patent is printed, double brackets indicate deletions and boldface indicates material added in the subject reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for notifying improper amendments and required supplemental oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 14.20.01 may be used to advise applicant of the proper manner of making amendments in a reissue application and to notify applicant of the need to file a supplemental oath/declaration before allowance for reissues filed before Sept 16, 2012. Form paragraph 14.21.01 may be used to notify applicant that proposed amendments filed before final rejection do not comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 14.21.01 sets a shortened statutory period (TWO MONTHS) for reply and should be used for pre-final-rejection informalities under 1.173(b). After final rejection, use an Advisory Office action (Form PTOL-303) indicating the amendment was not entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference and certificate of correction when parent issues without cross reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parent reissue application issues without any cross reissue application, amendment of the parent reissue patent to include a cross-reference to the continuation reissue application must be effected at the time of allowance of the continuation reissue application by certificate of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make an entry (e.g., in search notes or examiner’s amendment) referencing generation of a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.177(a) to provide notice of the continuation relationship between reissue patents.
